subject: Proof-of-Value checklist, exit gates, and fallback criteria
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Clara Hughes <clara@healthsync.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proof-of-Value checklist, acceptance tests, and exit gates (MAP v1)

Hi Clara —

Thanks again for carving out time to evaluate Redwood. Attached is a concise MAP and an initial set of acceptance tests so your team can validate fit during the two-week PoV. High-level items below; the full checklist is in HealthSync_MAP_v1.pdf and the test matrix is in acceptance_tests_v1.xlsx.

Key success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for interactive flows (50-150 tokens).
- Throughput: sustain 100 qps for 60% of peak windows for 72 continuous hours.
- Quality: intent concordance >= 92% against your evaluation set (see sheet: concordance_tests).
- Cost: per-request token costs within the target range we discussed (target: <= $0.006 per 1k input tokens for the workload profile).
- Security/compliance: VPC peering or private deployment option validated; SOC 2 evidence provided.

Exit gates (must be green to move toward contract close)
1) Functional: all critical smoke tests pass (auth, routing, basic prompts).
2) Performance: throughput and latency targets met in the stress window above.
3) Data controls: agreed retention and KMS config validated in a runbook.
4) Risk: no high-severity data leakage issues during fuzz testing.

Acceptance tests (summary)
- Smoke: auth, sample prompts, response schema.
- Concordance: 500 labelled prompts run; target >= 92% intent match.
- Load: 72-hour soak at target QPS with rolling restarts.
- Failover: simulate a node drop and confirm model fallback within 30s.
- Audit: confirm logs contain per-request trace IDs and redaction applied.

Fallback policy draft
- Primary: full model (redwood-alpha-1).
- Fallback: reduced-context quantized variant (redwood-alpha-1-q4) with smaller KV caching to keep latency <= 500ms.
- Auto-degrade trigger: sustained p95 > 500ms for 3 consecutive minutes or GPU node failure cascade.
(See redwood_fallback_policy.md attached for full detail.)

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): share MAP + tests (this email).
- Week 1: run smoke + concordance tests (customer provides anonymized eval set).
- Week 2: load soak + audit review; sign-off meeting at end of Week 2.

Actions for Clara
- Confirm the acceptance criteria above or call out changes by EOD Wed.
- Share anonymized evaluation set (or let us sign an NDA for raw samples).

Next steps from our side
- Neha will upload the test harness and coordinate the soak-run schedule.
- I’ll draft the DocuSign with the agreed PoV scope and a simple mutual action plan.

Attachments: HealthSync_MAP_v1.pdf, acceptance_tests_v1.xlsx, redwood_fallback_policy.md

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0113

From: Clara Hughes <clara@healthsync.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Contract Team <contracts@healthsync.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Proof-of-Value checklist, acceptance tests, and exit gates (MAP v1)

Thanks Marcus — this looks like a solid starting point. A few quick notes from my side: 

1) Timeline: can we extend the soak from 72 hours to 96 hours? We prefer a longer stability window before sign-off.
2) Data: we'll provide an anonymized eval set by Tuesday, but legal needs the NDA language you mentioned before handing over raw traces.
3) VPC: the SOC2 evidence is great; we will need VPC peering or a Private deployment option validated during the PoV. That must be in the exit gates.
4) Fallback: the fallback policy sounds reasonable, but can you confirm the behavioral difference in responses when the quantized variant is used (we need to ensure no regression on high-value prompts).

If you can incorporate these, I think we can proceed. I’ll loop in our infra lead if we need to coordinate peering.

Clara Hughes
Head of Integrations, HealthSync
clara@healthsync.com | +1 (212) 555-0222

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: HealthSync MAP feedback + ask: update tests & fallback plan

Team — forwarding Clara's notes. Two immediate asks:

1) Update acceptance_tests_v1.xlsx: change soak window to 96 hours and add a concordance regression check specifically for top-20 enterprise prompts.
2) Draft a short appendix explaining expected behavioral drift when the q4 quantized model is used (examples + sample prompts showing any likely truncation or phrasing differences). Clara wants assurance.
3) Confirm effort for VPC peering validation during PoV and whether we need infra support on HealthSync's side.

Owners / deadlines
- Neha: update test matrix and compile a short behavior-drift appendix (by Tue EOD 12/01).
- Aditya: I'll work with sales ops to get the NDA and a clean DocuSign scope; can you review the contractual scope and cost guardrails? (by Tue noon).

If we can meet those, I’ll send an updated MAP and the DocuSign link to Clara. Also planning to include the fallback policy doc as a companion.

Marcus
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: HealthSync MAP feedback + ask: update tests & fallback plan

Adding technical notes and timeline:

- Soak window: bumping to 96h is fine. We should schedule it to start Friday 12/04 00:00 PST to avoid heavy weekday traffic; that gives HealthSync time to share the anonymized set.
- Behavior drift: quantized model q4 can introduce minor phrasing changes on long generative tails and lower-probability tokens — in practice we see ~1.8% decrease in concordance on enterprise NLU prompts vs. full model in our benchmarks. I'll attach a 1-pager with sample before/after responses (redwood_fallback_policy.md).
- VPC peering: we can validate peering during PoV; required items from HealthSync: CIDR block, endpoint approvals, and a temporary access window for our infra team (we'll document steps in the MAP appendix). Estimated effort: 4 engineer-hours to validate + 2 hours for coordination.
- Test harness: I'll push the harness to the shared bucket and populate the acceptance_tests_v1.xlsx with the top-20 prompt subset and the concordance scoring script.

Deliverables (Neha) by Tue EOD 12/01:
- acceptance_tests_v1.xlsx (updated)
- redwood_fallback_policy.md (1-pager + sample responses)
- runbook snippet for VPC peering validation

I’ll queue the soak run once Clara confirms the anonymized dataset delivery timeline.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
